title: runtime/tests: add regression coverage for bursty mixed-length traffic that triggers KV cache fragmentation tails
author: Marcus Reed
description: Context: We’ve had multiple reports (and the 2025-02-11 incident) where bursty arrivals + mixed sequence lengths cause the KV cache allocator to accumulate holes, increasing allocation/eviction churn and producing p95/p99 spikes. This PR adds regression tests that deterministically reproduce the pre-fix behavior when compaction is disabled, and provides an A/B harness to validate improvements when compaction is enabled. Why now: The allocator/compaction PR series needs a stable, repeatable gate for “bursty-mix tail latency + fragmentation” so we don’t regress in future kernel/scheduler changes. What’s included: (1) New scenario generator for bursty arrivals with a configurable length distribution (short decode-heavy + occasional long context prefill) and a fixed RNG seed, (2) A simulator-backed regression test that drives the real KV block-map allocator via the runtime’s allocation interface (no GPU required) and asserts fragmentation + churn signatures are present with compaction=off, (3) An optional GPU integration test (quarantined by default in CI) that runs the same workload against a tiny test model and records p95/p99 + allocation failures to artifacts; it’s intended for perf-canary and manual verification, not as a per-PR gating check, (4) Golden thresholds + output artifacts: fragmentation_ratio, alloc_failures, evictions/sec, and compaction_bytes_moved (expected 0 when compaction disabled). Expected behavior: With compaction disabled, the simulator test should reliably exceed fragmentation_ratio >= 0.22 within 90s of synthetic time and show elevated “realloc_attempts” during burst windows (this is the pre-fix signature). With compaction enabled (flag on), the same harness is expected to keep fragmentation_ratio <= 0.12 and reduce realloc_attempts; we record these stats but do not hard-gate on them yet (until the compaction engine + budgets fully land on main). How to run: (A) Fast regression: bazel test //runtime/tests/kv_cache:kv_cache_fragmentation_bursty_mix_test (B) GPU (manual): bazel test //runtime/tests/kv_cache:kv_cache_fragmentation_bursty_mix_gpu_itest --test_arg=--enable_compaction=[0|1] --test_arg=--artifacts_dir=/tmp/kvfrag Notes / guardrails: The simulator uses the same block sizing and eviction hooks as runtime, but it bypasses kernels; the goal is to guard allocator/scheduler contract invariants and fragmentation dynamics without needing GPU determinism. The GPU integration test is marked as “non-gating” and requires the GPU runners. Follow-ups: After PRs 18457/18481/18490 land broadly, we should tighten the enabled-compaction assertions and make at least one enabled-compaction check gating in nightly/perf-canary.
commits: test(kv-cache): add bursty mixed-length scenario generator + fixed seed
test(kv-cache): add simulator regression for fragmentation + churn signatures
test(kv-cache): add optional GPU integration test + artifact uploader
build: wire new targets into runtime test suites (non-gating by default)
docs(testing): add notes on running bursty-mix tests and interpreting outputs
snippet:
New regression assertions (simulator):
- Run 6 burst windows over 90s synthetic time, length dist: p50=256, p90=2k, p99=12k tokens
- Assert fragmentation_ratio_max >= 0.22 with compaction=0 (repro signature)
- Assert alloc_failures == 0 (this is a regression test, not an OOM test)
- Assert realloc_attempts_per_min >= 30 during burst windows
- Collect JSON artifact: {fragmentation_ratio_ts, evictions_ts, realloc_attempts_ts}

GPU integration (non-gating):
- Record p95/p99 decode latency and allocator failure counters
- Upload artifacts when RUN_GPU_NON_GATING=1
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed: Can we avoid hard-coding the 0.22 fragmentation threshold? It might move when we change block size in ADR-0127. Suggest basing the assertion on a relative increase vs warm baseline (e.g., +0.15) and/or leaving a single constant in one header so we can tune once.

Marcus Reed: Good point. I moved thresholds into kv_cache_fragmentation_thresholds.h and changed the main assertion to (frag_peak - frag_at_t0) >= 0.15 with a minimum absolute floor of 0.18 to keep it meaningful. Also added a comment referencing ADR-0127 so we remember to revisit after block size changes.

Rina Kobayashi: For the GPU test, please make sure it cannot accidentally run on normal PR CI (we’ve had flakes from GPU runner contention). Also can we emit the same JSON schema as the simulator so perf-canary can ingest without special casing?

Marcus Reed: Updated: GPU target is now tagged requires-gpu and only wired into ci/test_suites/runtime_gpu_non_gating.yaml. Also standardized the artifact schema (kvfrag_metrics_v1.json) across sim + GPU.

Grace Kim: One concern: the scenario uses prefill/decode interleaving; if someone changes scheduler heuristics, the burst windows may shift and break determinism. Can we pin the synthetic arrival schedule independent of scheduler ordering?

Marcus Reed: I pinned the arrival schedule to wall-clock “synthetic time” and made request generation independent of scheduler ordering (scheduler only consumes a queue). Added a deterministic tie-breaker on request_id for any ordering-sensitive code paths in the test harness.
Kira Volkov: Please add a note in the doc about how to interpret realloc_attempts vs alloc_failures and that alloc_failures must remain 0 for this regression suite.
Marcus Reed: Added to docs/eng/runtime/testing/kv_cache_fragmentation_regressions.md and to the test failure messages.
release_notes: Internal: Added deterministic regression coverage for KV cache fragmentation tails under bursty mixed-length traffic (simulator gating + optional GPU artifact test).
